page.layout: One page of text, full width. At the top: running head "IEREMIÆ." with the page number 31 at the right. Below it, a centred heading "COPH. RESCH. SCHIN.". Then a verse stanza of 18 lines. Below a rule, a centred heading "TAV.", a centred title line "Carmina sunt ex superioribus mixta.", and a verse passage of 3 lines with a large initial H. No margin notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.head: COPH. RESCH. SCHIN.
main_text.p: SEDte Sancte Parens, speluncis abdita cæcis Vndarumq; alto vortice mersa voco. Aure etenim miti vocem exaudire precantum, Atque piæ gentis vota iuuare soles. Ostendis, quoties supplex tua Numina posco, Præsens auxilium, meque timere vetas. Te measumme Deus stat iusto vindice causa: Tuta patrocinio nunc mihi vita tuo est. Ecce vides cæli celso de vertice, acerbus Hostis ut immeritam me premat vsque malis. Artes, insidias, crudelia pectora, fraudes, Atque vides quantis me petat ille dolis. Audis me quanto molimine perdere certet: Audis & illius scommata, probra, iocos. Et quæ verba crepat, quæ sæuo corde volutat Consilia, & quantas nocte, dieque neces. Stet, sedeátue[?] illi sum fabula grata, suique Me nunc materiem carminis esse facit.
main_text.head: TAV.
Carmina sunt ex superioribus mixta.
main_text.p: HOstes sed paribus concutias verberibus tuos Deus benigne vindex: Supplicisque illorum immania facta rependas

page.notes: The initial S of the first stanza and the initial H of the Tav passage are large letters, joined to the first word as SEDte and HOstes. "cæcis" may be "cacis" in print (the ligature is unclear). "sedeátue" is doubtful: the scan shows a mark over the a, and the word may be sedeatue or sedeatque. The running head IEREMIÆ. is printed above a rule; the line COPH. RESCH. SCHIN. is a title of the passage, not a running head. Long s is transcribed as s throughout. The line "Tuta patrocinio" may be read as "Tutapatrocinio" in print, but I have divided it as the sense requires. The verse lines are kept inside one paragraph per stanza, not one per line.
